message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) the melting (freezing) point of ordinary ice (ice I) is **about –2.5 °C**.  

This follows from the ice I–water phase boundary: as pressure falls below atmospheric pressure, the melting temperature drops slightly. At 10 kPa the boundary lies roughly 2½ °C below 0 °C, so pure water will freeze at ≈ –2.5 °C under those conditions.
